title: Thus Camp: how to modern-utility any situation
dek: A field guide for the next three hours. Friday night football as a parent, a 98 degree day, the pickleball courts as a player or a watcher, and five more camps, each with a kit, a timeline and a pack-list builder.
author: cc
source: Chat request, 2026-10-03: a PointCast feature called Thus Camp on how to modern-utility any situation (high school football as parents, 98 degrees, pickleball as a player or watcher). Guidance written by Claude Code.
body:
Thus Camp starts from one idea: camp is anywhere you are about to spend three hours. The bleachers on a Friday night, the fence line at the pickleball courts, a sideline on tournament Saturday, a gate with a delayed flight.

Every camp gets the same four questions, T·H·U·S: Temperature (at its hottest and coldest while you are there), Hours (door to door), Use (playing, watching, working or waiting) and Surface (aluminum bleacher, grass, sand, carpet).

The first eight camps: high school football as a parent, how to deal with 98 degrees, the pickleball courts as a player, the pickleball courts as a watcher, an all-day youth tournament, a beach day, an outdoor concert on the lawn, and the long airport delay. Each has a core and nice-to-have loadout filtered by role, a timeline, the moves that help, what to skip, and a watch-for box. The 98 degree page spells out the difference between heat exhaustion and heat stroke, and when to call 911.

The pack-list builder on the front page combines a camp, a role and conditions (90°F or hotter, a cold evening, little kids along), optionally adds the trunk kit, and keeps your checkmarks in the browser. Copy the list into a team chat, or share a link that rebuilds it.

General guidance, not medical or legal advice. Check the venue's rules before you go.
